cards.prose: The householder sowed good seed, and *while men slept* his enemy came and sowed the tares. Genesis shows the hour. Men began to multiply and daughters were born, and the verse after it says *the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair* (Genesis 6:2). Nobody in the field was watching when the other seed went in.
cards.member_sentence: Men multiply on the earth and daughters are born, the opening of the hour when the enemy's seed was sown among them.

cards.prose: The tares were sown by an enemy who *went his way* once the work was done. In the garden his work is a question put to the woman, *hath Elohim (God) said*, and from that first tree the enemy's seed runs on in the line of Adam. What the householder finds in the field was begun there.
cards.member_phrase: And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath Elohim (God) said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
cards.member_sentence: The serpent's first words to the woman put what Elohim (God) had said in doubt, the enemy sowing his seed in the garden.
cards.flag: Chose the 2 Esdras seed thread over the Genesis 3 seed-war thread; both fit, this one names the evil seed sown in Adam.

cards.prose: The King says the tares are *the children of the wicked one*, and here he tells particular men standing in front of him whose father they are, a murderer from the beginning and the father of lies. He says it to those who would not hear his word, not to the whole people. A tare is known by its father.
cards.member_phrase: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) names the father of men who would not hear him, the plain statement that some in the crowd are children of the wicked one.

cards.prose: John writes from the other side of the same field. The devil has been at his work from the beginning, and the Son of Elohim (God) appeared to put an end to what he built. The tares in the parable are his children, which is why the Son of Adam clears them out at the harvest.
cards.member_sentence: John says the devil has worked from the beginning and the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed to undo his works.
cards.flag: The packet's text of 1 John 3:8 reads like a modern rendering, not the restored KJV; I used WHOLE and kept my prose off its wording.

cards.prose: Here a tare stands inside the field wearing the field's own colors. These are a priest's sons, born in the chosen line, and they are *sons of Belial*, men who did not know Yahuah (the LORD). The *children of the wicked one* are not only out among the nations. Some were sown into the house itself.
cards.member_sentence: Priest's sons born in the chosen line are called sons of Belial who knew not Yahuah (the LORD), a tare sown inside the house.

cards.prose: The wheat is gathered into the barn, but gathered wheat does not go straight home. Yahuah (the LORD) says here that he will *rule over you* with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and the verses that follow bring the house out of the countries to the wilderness. *And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.* (Ezekiel 20:35)
cards.member_phrase: surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) will rule over the scattered house with a mighty hand and bring it into the wilderness to be tried face to face.

cards.prose: The Son of Adam sends his angels to gather out of *his kingdom* all that offends and does iniquity. Ezekiel shows what the clearing is for. Yahuah (the LORD) will rule over the house he scattered, and he says he will gather it: *I will bring you out from the people, and will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered* (Ezekiel 20:34). Clearing and gathering are one work.
cards.member_phrase: surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) declares he will rule over the house he scattered, the rule that clears the kingdom and gathers his people home.
cards.flag: Ezekiel 20:33 also serves the 13:30 card; I put this one with the gathering of the scattered house, since the verse leads straight into the gathering.

cards.prose: The angels gather out *them which do iniquity*, and the Sermon holds the same measure over everyone who calls him *Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord)*. The one who enters is *he that doeth the will of my Father*. Naming him is not the standard. Doing what the Father said is.
cards.member_phrase: but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven
cards.member_sentence: Lawlessness is the measure: only the one who does the will of the Father enters, whatever he calls the King.
cards.flag: I did not say the Matthew 7:21 warning falls on the tares; it falls on those who call him Lord, which is wheat that must bear fruit.

cards.prose: In the parable the tares are taken out first and burned. John sets the second step beside it. Once the wheat is in, the fan goes through the floor and the chaff is burned with fire that cannot be put out. Those are two clearings, one after the other, and the wheat comes through both.
cards.member_sentence: John says the coming one clears his floor, keeps the wheat in his garner, and burns the chaff with unquenchable fire.

cards.prose: The righteous shine in the kingdom of *their Father*, and here the King calls them *blessed of my Father* and says the kingdom was made ready for them from the foundation of the world. The shining at the end of the field is the inheritance of people whose place was prepared before anything was sown.
cards.member_sentence: The King welcomes the blessed to a kingdom prepared for them from the foundation of the world.

cards.prose: Both grow together until the harvest, and Zechariah shows what the harvest does to the land: *two parts therein shall be cut off and die*, and the third is left. Standing in the field was never the same as being wheat, and the fire the third part passes through is what shows the difference.
cards.member_phrase: two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein
cards.member_sentence: In all the land two parts are cut off and die and a third is left, so being born in the field is not enough.

cards.prose: In the parable the reapers are the angels, and they take up the tares first. Here the Son of Adam sends the same angels out with a great trumpet, and what they gather is *his elect from the four winds*. The harvest clears the field and it also brings the chosen in from every direction.
cards.member_phrase: they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other
cards.member_sentence: The Son of Adam sends his angels with a trumpet to gather his elect from the four winds.

cards.prose: The disciples ask for the parable of the tares to be declared, and he tells them the harvest is the end and the reapers are angels. John sees it. On a white cloud sits one *like unto the Son of Adam*, a golden crown on his head and a sharp sickle in his hand, and the time to reap has come.
cards.member_phrase: upon the cloud one sat like unto the Son of Adam, having on his head a golden crown, and in his hand a sharp sickle
cards.member_sentence: John sees the harvest of the earth: one like the Son of Adam on a white cloud with a crown and a sharp sickle.
cards.flag: Map thread for this card does not exist; used the tares and harvest thread. The kaph (like unto) is kept as written.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says he speaks in parables *because they seeing see not*, and the words behind that are Isaiah's. The prophet is sent to *this people* with a word to hear indeed and not understand. The parables are given the way that word was given, so that this people hear and do not understand.
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah is sent to this people with the word to hear indeed and not understand, the commission Matthew says the parables fulfil.

cards.prose: The mysteries are given to some, and to others it is *not given*. The Shepherd says the reason in his own words: *ye are not of my sheep*. Then he adds, *My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me* (John 10:27). The giving comes before the hearing, and the hearing shows whose they were.
cards.member_sentence: Those who believe not are not of his sheep, the sheep being the ones who hear.

cards.prose: Paul says a man left to his own nature takes in nothing of the Spirit of Elohim (God), because *they are spiritually discerned*. It is the same line the King draws. The mysteries are given to some, and to others they sound foolish. It is not a matter of being clever enough to find them.
cards.member_phrase: the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of Elohim (God): for they are foolishness unto him
cards.member_sentence: The natural man cannot receive the things of the Spirit of Elohim (God); they are foolishness to him and are spiritually discerned.
cards.flag: Kept the natural man from being equated with the tares; the verse does not say that.

cards.prose: Matthew says Isaiah's word is fulfilled in them, and John gives the same reading of the crowd. They had seen so many miracles and *they believed not on him*, and John goes straight on: *Therefore they could not believe, because that Esaias said again* (John 12:39). The unbelief was no surprise. It was what the prophet had said would be.
cards.member_sentence: Though he did so many miracles before them they believed not, and John answers it with Isaiah.

cards.prose: At Rome Paul gives the speaker of the very words Matthew quotes: the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke them *by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers*. So this is an old word, not a new charge. The room divided there as the crowd by the sea did, and some went away disagreeing among themselves.
cards.member_phrase: Well spake the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke the word about hearing without understanding through Isaiah to the fathers, as his hearers at Rome parted.

cards.prose: Isaiah says they hear and do not understand. Paul says who: Yashar'el (Israel) sought and did not obtain, *but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded*. The blinding falls on the rest. Those who see were the election before they looked, and the crowd by the sea shows the two sides.
cards.member_phrase: but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded
cards.member_sentence: Yashar'el (Israel) did not obtain what it sought; the election obtained it and the rest were blinded.

cards.prose: Blessed are the eyes that see, he tells the disciples, and Peter shows what that blessing cost others. The prophets *enquired and searched diligently* about this very salvation. Many of them waited and died before it came. These men are standing in the thing they longed to see.
cards.member_sentence: The prophets searched diligently into the salvation the disciples are now seeing.

cards.prose: It is given to some and not to others, and Daniel says that is how it has always gone. Elohim (God) changes the times and the seasons, removes kings and sets up kings, and *giveth wisdom unto the wise*. Wisdom is handed out by the one who gives it. It is not picked up by the cleverest.
cards.member_phrase: he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge to them that know understanding
cards.member_sentence: Elohim (God) is the one who gives wisdom and knowledge, which is why the mysteries are given to some.

cards.prose: The net gathers *of every kind*, and the sorting is done at the shore. He has already shown the disciples what that sorting looks like. They asked for *the parable of the tares of the field*, and he told them the harvest is the end and the reapers are angels. The net is the same teaching in another picture.
cards.member_sentence: The disciples ask for the parable of the tares to be declared, the explanation the net repeats in another picture.
cards.flag: Same chapter, so the target is the explanation of the tares; I joined it to the net thread since the card is anchored at the net.

cards.prose: He called them with *fishers of men*, and here the net is cast into the sea and brings in everything. Casting it wide is the work he gave them. Sorting what comes up is not, because that is done at the shore by the angels.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) calls the first disciples to follow him and become fishers of men, the work of the net.

cards.prose: The net is drawn in and sorted, and the wicked are severed first. After that, Ezekiel's river brings life to everything it touches, and where the sea is healed there is *a very great multitude of fish*. The sorting at the shore comes before the healed waters of the reign.
cards.member_phrase: there shall be a very great multitude of fish, because these waters shall come thither
cards.member_sentence: Where the river's waters come the sea is healed and a great multitude of fish live in it.

cards.prose: *The angels shall come forth* and sever the wicked from the just, and here the Son of Adam comes on the throne of his glory with all the holy angels to divide sheep from goats. Both are the sorting of what has been gathered, the seed brought out of every nation and sifted, rather than the nations judged for a place in the reign.
cards.member_sentence: The Son of Adam comes in glory with the holy angels to sit on his throne and divide the gathered.
cards.flag: The old note reads Matthew 25 as the sorting of the gathered seed, not nations judged for entry; I kept it, though verse 32 says all nations are gathered before him.

cards.prose: The wicked are severed from among the just, and Daniel says how deep the sorting goes. The sleepers in the dust wake, *some to everlasting life*, and the others *to shame and everlasting contempt*. The angels' work reaches down to the graves, and the two ways out are not alike.
cards.member_sentence: Many who sleep in the dust awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

cards.prose: A woman hides leaven in three measures of meal until the whole is leavened. Torah says what leaven is: at the feast ye *put away leaven out of your houses*, and whoever eats it in those days is cut off from Yashar'el (Israel). This reads the picture as something getting into the meal that has to be removed, not welcomed.
cards.member_phrase: for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Yashar'el (Israel)
cards.member_sentence: Leaven is put out of the house at the feast and the one who eats it is cut off from Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.flag: The old notes read the leaven as corruption, not growth; I kept that and wrote it as a reading, since the usual pulpit reading of this parable is the opposite.

cards.prose: Leaven is hid in the meal, and the Torah says no meal offering brought to Yahuah (the LORD) may be made with leaven. The woman does with her meal the one thing the altar does not allow. So the picture is not of something clean being added to the meal.
cards.member_phrase: No meat offering, which ye shall bring unto Yahuah (LORD), shall be made with leaven
cards.member_sentence: No meal offering brought to Yahuah (the LORD) may be made with leaven, so leaven in the meal is out of place.

cards.prose: When he speaks of leaven again it is a warning: *beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees*. Leaven in his own mouth is something to watch for. So the woman and her three measures can be heard that way, with a small thing working its way through the whole meal.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) tells the disciples to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the Sadducees.

cards.prose: The disciples thought he meant bread. He tells them he did not speak *concerning bread*, and the verse after it says the leaven is the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees. Leaven is his word for something that starts small and works through the whole lump.
cards.member_phrase: that I spake it not to you concerning bread, that ye should beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees
cards.member_sentence: He was not speaking of bread but warning them against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which the next verse calls their teaching.

cards.prose: Luke has him name it in one word. The leaven of the Pharisees, *which is hypocrisy*, is hid in the meal and works through the whole lump. It is keeping that is only for show. The system is named plainly and the people under it are not mocked.
cards.member_phrase: Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples first of all to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

cards.prose: Paul puts it as a rule: *a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump*. The woman hid only a little in three measures, and the parable ends with all of it leavened. He says it to people whose glorying is not good, so the small thing allowed to stay is what spoils the lump.
cards.member_sentence: A little leaven leavens the whole lump, said to people whose glorying was not good.

cards.prose: Paul says it again to Galatia: *A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump*. He has just said the persuasion among them does not come from the one who calls them. A small teaching let in can work through a whole assembly, and the three measures show how little it takes.
cards.member_sentence: A little leaven leavens the whole lump, said of the persuasion that was hindering the Galatians from obeying the truth.

cards.prose: Three measures of fine meal is what Abraham told Sarah to make ready when guests came to his tent and he hurried to feed them. The woman in the parable hides her leaven in that same quantity. It is the meal of a covenant house that the leaven is put into.
cards.member_sentence: Abraham has Sarah make ready three measures of fine meal for his guests, the quantity the woman's leaven is hid in.
cards.flag: Old note says the meal was prepared for Yahuah's visit; the verse and context given do not say who the guests are, so I wrote guests.

cards.prose: The same words close the sower and the tares. *Who hath ears to hear, let him hear* is said first over seed that fell on every kind of ground, and again over the righteous shining in the kingdom of their Father. The hearing in the soil and the shining at the end are one road.
cards.member_sentence: He repeats the call to hear at the end of the tares' explanation, after the righteous shine in the kingdom of their Father.

cards.prose: Having ears is a gift, and Moses says on that day it had not been given. After all they had seen, Yahuah (the LORD) *hath not given you an heart to perceive*. He says it to all Yashar'el (Israel). So when he says let him hear, he knows the hearing is given.
cards.member_sentence: Moses tells all Yashar'el (Israel) that Yahuah (the LORD) had not yet given them a heart to perceive, eyes to see, or ears to hear.

cards.prose: The mysteries are given to the disciples, and Paul calls what he speaks *the hidden wisdom*, which Elohim (God) ordained *before the world unto our glory*. It was settled before there was a world. That is why it is given and cannot be found.
cards.member_sentence: Paul speaks the hidden wisdom of Elohim (God) in a mystery, ordained before the world.

cards.prose: Paul does not claim to have worked the mystery out. He says *by revelation he made known unto me the mystery*. That is how a mystery of the kingdom reaches anyone: it is made known to them, the way it is given to the disciples here while the crowd gets parables.
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the mystery was made known to him by revelation, not by his own working.

cards.prose: He speaks in parables because they see and do not see. John says what that looked like in the crowd. After so many miracles *they believed not on him*. Seeing the works without seeing him is exactly what the parable-speech describes.
cards.member_sentence: Though he had done so many miracles before them, they believed not on him.

cards.prose: They see and do not see, hear and do not understand. At Rome Paul puts a name to the one who first said it: the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke it through Isaiah to the fathers. It is an old word about this people, not a new charge, and the hearers there parted ways over it.
cards.member_phrase: Well spake the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers
cards.member_sentence: Paul at Rome says the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke the word about seeing without perceiving by Isaiah to the fathers.

cards.prose: Seeing they see not describes Yashar'el (Israel) when Paul wrote. The house sought what it did not obtain, and *the election hath obtained it*, while the rest were blinded. Those who do not understand the parables are the rest. Those who do were the election before the telling.
cards.member_phrase: but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded
cards.member_sentence: The election obtained what Yashar'el (Israel) sought, and the rest were blinded.

cards.prose: He gave the crowd the story of the good seed and the field. In the house the disciples ask him to declare it, *the parable of the tares of the field*. What the crowd got as a picture the disciples get as a plain account, one piece at a time.
cards.member_sentence: The disciples ask him in the house to declare the parable of the tares, and he gives them the plain account.
cards.flag: Map guess was the 2 Esdras seed thread; this pair is Matthew explaining his own parable, so I used the tares and harvest thread anchored on these verses.

cards.prose: The man sowed good seed in his field. Genesis shows the field filling: *when men began to multiply on the face of the earth*. Into that earth came the sons of Elohim (God), who *came in unto the daughters of men* (Genesis 6:4). The enemy's seed went in among the good.
cards.member_sentence: Men multiplied on the earth and daughters were born, the field the good seed was sown in.

cards.prose: Good seed is sown first in the householder's field, and the trouble comes by a voice that talks. The serpent comes to the woman in the garden and puts the sower's own word in doubt. The enemy of the parable begins by making the word look like something that might not have been said.
cards.member_phrase: And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath Elohim (God) said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
cards.member_sentence: The serpent asks the woman whether Elohim (God) really said it, the enemy's first move against the sown word.
cards.flag: Map thread for this card does not exist; used the seed war thread rather than the 2 Esdras one.

cards.prose: A small seed grows into a tree where the birds of the air lodge, and Yahuah (the LORD) says he will crop a tender twig from the top of the cedar and plant it on a high mountain. The next verse names the place: *In the mountain of the height of Yashar'el (Israel) will I plant it* (Ezekiel 17:23). The little beginning is something he plants himself.
cards.member_phrase: I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) takes a tender twig and plants it on the high mountain of Yashar'el (Israel), where it becomes a great tree.

cards.prose: A tree with *the fowls of the heaven* in its boughs is how Daniel's page draws a kingdom. This one stood in the midst of the earth with food for all flesh until a watcher came down and called for it to be hewn. The mustard tree is set among the same pictures.
cards.member_phrase: the beasts of the field had shadow under it, and the fowls of the heaven dwelt in the boughs thereof, and all flesh was fed of it
cards.member_sentence: Nebuchadnezzar's great tree shelters the beasts and the fowls of heaven and feeds all flesh, the picture of a kingdom.

cards.prose: Ezekiel's great tree had *all the fowls of heaven* nesting in its boughs, and under its shadow *dwelt all great nations*. That is how a grown kingdom is drawn. When the least of seeds becomes a tree with birds in its branches, the listener already has these pictures in mind.
cards.member_sentence: Ezekiel's great tree has the fowls of heaven nesting in its boughs and great nations dwelling in its shadow.

cards.prose: He spoke to the crowd only in parables, and this is the psalm being filled. The psalmist opens his mouth in a parable and utters *dark sayings of old*. What Yahusha (Jesus) says by the sea is not new speech. It is the old dark saying handed to the fathers' children, now spoken aloud.
cards.member_sentence: The psalmist opens his mouth in a parable and utters dark sayings of old, the word Yahusha (Jesus) takes up.

cards.prose: Paul speaks of a mystery *kept secret since the world began*, and then says it *is made manifest, and by the scriptures of the prophets* (Romans 16:26). What Yahusha (Jesus) says only in parables is that same hidden thing, and it was never apart from the prophets.
cards.member_phrase: according to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the mystery kept secret since the world began is now made manifest through the scriptures of the prophets.

cards.prose: They ask him to declare the parable, and he says who the tares are. In John he says it plainly to men standing in front of him: their father is the devil. A tare has a father just as the wheat has one, and the explanation in the house turns on that.
cards.member_phrase: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do
cards.member_sentence: He tells the men before him their father is the devil, a murderer from the beginning, the plain form of the tares' explanation.
cards.flag: Map thread does not exist; used the seed war thread.

cards.prose: The disciples ask for the tares to be explained, and John gives the line that sorts them: *In this the children of Elohim (God) are manifest, and the children of the devil* (1 John 3:10). Fruit shows which are which. And the Son of Elohim (God) came to put an end to the devil's works, so the field is not left to him.
cards.member_sentence: Children of Elohim (God) and children of the devil are made manifest, and the Son of Elohim (God) came to undo the devil's works.
cards.flag: The packet's 1 John 3:8 text looks modernised; I quoted only 3:10 from the context given.

cards.prose: The explanation of the tares ends with the righteous shining like the sun, and Daniel has the picture first: *shall shine as the brightness of the firmament*. The meaning of the tares ends in a shining that was already promised to the wise and to those who turn many to righteousness.
cards.member_phrase: they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament
cards.member_sentence: Daniel says the wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament and those who turn many to righteousness as the stars.

cards.prose: Declare the parable, they asked, and the end of his answer is a kingdom for the righteous. The King says the same later to the sheep on his right hand, *prepared for you from the foundation of the world*. The wheat does not earn that place at the end. It was made ready long before the field was sown.
cards.member_sentence: The King calls the blessed to inherit a kingdom prepared for them from the foundation of the world.
cards.flag: Map thread does not exist; used the tares and harvest thread.

cards.prose: The man who finds the treasure sells all he has to buy the field. Isaiah shows who pays for Yashar'el (Israel). Yahuah (the LORD) says *Since thou wast precious in my sight*, and so he will give men and peoples for the life of his own. The treasure is what he already counted precious.
cards.member_sentence: Because Yashar'el (Israel) was precious in his sight, Yahuah (the LORD) gives men and peoples for its life.

cards.prose: The man gives up all he has to get the field. Paul writes of one who, being in the form of Elohim (God), *made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant* (Philippians 2:7). He let go of what was his in order to take what he came for.
cards.member_sentence: He who was in the form of Elohim (God) gave up what was his and took the form of a servant.

cards.prose: The treasure is hid in a field and bought with everything the man has. Moses tells what Yahuah (the LORD) calls his own treasure, a holy people chosen *to be a special people unto himself*. It was not their number that moved him, since *ye were the fewest of all people* (Deuteronomy 7:7).
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) has chosen a holy people to be a special people to himself, above all peoples on the earth.

cards.prose: The net gathers *of every kind*, and the sorting happens at the shore. The Son of Adam on his throne does the same with sheep and goats: everything brought before him is divided, one from another. The gathering comes first and the dividing second, and the dividing is his work, not the fishermen's.
cards.member_sentence: The Son of Adam sits on his throne of glory to divide the gathered, as the net is sorted at the shore.

cards.prose: Everything is drawn to shore and then sorted. Daniel shows two outcomes in the graves as well. Of the many who sleep in the dust, some wake *to everlasting life* and some *to shame and everlasting contempt*. What the net sorts on the shore, the dust sorts in the earth.
cards.member_sentence: Many who sleep in the dust awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

cards.prose: The scribe instructed in the kingdom brings out of his treasure things new and old, and the old is not thrown away for the new. *I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil*, the Sermon says of the law and the prophets. The commandments stay in the householder's house.
cards.member_sentence: He did not come to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfil them, so the old stays in the treasure.

cards.prose: The old is kept in the new. Paul says *I delight in the law of Elohim (God)*, and he says it of the inward man. That is the scribe of the kingdom bringing out what is old and loving it. The law is not what he is rescued from. It is what he delights in within.
cards.member_sentence: Paul delights in the law of Elohim (God) after the inward man, the old held in the new heart.

cards.prose: The new covenant Jeremiah promises is not a different law. Yahuah (the LORD) says he will put his law within them and *write it in their hearts*. What is new is the place of the writing, and what is written is the old. That is what the householder's treasure holds, new and old together.
cards.member_phrase: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts
cards.member_sentence: In the new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel) the same law is put in their inward parts and written on their hearts.

cards.prose: In his own country they know his mother and his brothers by name and cannot get past that. John says *neither did his brethren believe in him*, so the offence in Nazareth was close to home. It came from the people of his own house, as he says it does.
cards.member_sentence: Even his brothers did not believe in him, the offence in his own house.

cards.prose: Mark tells the same visit. He came into *his own country* with his disciples following, and the people who knew his family were offended at him. Knowing his mother and his brothers was not the same as hearing him.
cards.member_sentence: Mark records the same return to his own country and the offence of those who knew his family.

cards.prose: Luke has him at Nazareth, where he had been brought up, in the synagogue on the sabbath *as his custom was*. The people in Matthew are no strangers. They had watched him keep the sabbath all his life, and what they stumble over is the man standing up to read.
cards.member_phrase: he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read
cards.member_sentence: At Nazareth, where he was raised, he goes into the synagogue on the sabbath as his custom was and stands to read.

cards.prose: A prophet is not honoured in his own country, and Jeremiah knew it. The men of Anathoth, his own townsmen, told him *Prophesy not in the name of Yahuah (LORD)* and sought his life. It is an old pattern. The word comes to its own house and the house will not have it.
cards.member_phrase: thus saith Yahuah (LORD) of the men of Anathoth, that seek thy life, saying, Prophesy not in the name of Yahuah (LORD)
cards.member_sentence: The men of Anathoth, Jeremiah's own townsmen, seek his life and tell him not to prophesy in the name of Yahuah (the LORD).
